findings.location: Statement opening parenthetical concrete witness; Facts F1–F2; Verification 1.1
findings.evidence: The conditional calculation assumes genus two, a degree-five quotient and H_1(X;Z)=A·C free of rank one. The named regular-pentagon/algebraic curve is advertised as satisfying these hypotheses, but F1–F2 take them as Given and no listed supplier constructs C or proves its orbit is an integral basis for that concrete curve. McMullen, Chapter 15, printed p. 128, confirms the classical assertion but leaves the polygon homology computation implicit. Supply a local cell/branched-cover witness establishing the integral module, genus, quotient and identification of the two models; the conditional period argument is not disputed.

findings.location: Statement clause 3, covolume |det M|; Verification 5.1, final covolume assertion
findings.evidence: M is never defined. Covolume requires a real 4-by-4 matrix of the four period vectors under an explicit C^2-to-R^4 coordinate convention; the displayed complex Vandermonde matrix is not that real basis matrix. Define M with the real and imaginary coordinate columns before asserting covolume |det M|.

findings.location: Facts F7; Verification 5.1, Vandermonde invertibility attributed to F7
findings.evidence: The opened thm-invertible-matrix-theorem gives equivalences between invertibility, trivial kernel and other conditions; it does not establish the Vandermonde condition asserted in F7. The immediate missing derivation is that a real relation defines a polynomial of degree at most three vanishing at four distinct fifth roots, hence is zero. Add that argument or a justified determinant product. This short omission is nonfatal.
